newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi brother denies trying to discredit Di Pietro.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi brother denies trying to discredit Di Pietro.

text.p: The brother of former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi denied on Wednesday that he had plotted to discredit an ex-magistrate who shot to fame by leading a judicial assault on corruption in high places.

Paolo Berlusconi was testifying at a trial in which he and former defence minister Cesare Previti are charged with orchestrating a plot to besmirch the reputation of Antonio Di Pietro, a folk hero in Italy.

Di Pietro quit as a magistrate in December 1994 for reasons that have never been explained. He resigned two months ago as public works minister when he himself came under investigation for alleged irregularities in his work as a magistrate.
The Berlusconis have been at the centre of several investigations into graft carried out by the pool of Milan magistrates which Di Pietro spearheaded before his sudden resignation.

Silvio Berlusconi is now on trial in Milan in two separate corruption cases linked to his media empire and which were investigated by Di Pietro and the "Clean Hands" pool of investigators. He denies all charges.

Paolo Berlusconi, a close business associate of his brother, said he learned in the summer of 1994 that Di Pietro was planning to leave the magistrature as a prelude to launching a career in politics. That preceded the time when when prosecutors say a plot to pressure Di Pietro into resigning was hatched.

Berlusconi said it was not until some months later that he advised Giancarlo Gorrini, then a friend of Di Pietro, to report alleged malpractices by the star magistrate to government inspectors probing the activities of the Milan magistrates.
Gorrini had alleged that Di Pietro extracted a 100 million lire ($65,000) loan from him and then pressured him into providing a Mercedes car and work for his lawyer wife.

His allegations formed the basis of a judicial investigation into Di Pietro last year after which a court ruled there was no evidence of wrongdoing by the former magistrate. Di Pietro is now under investigation again following separate allegations.
